fact: Colony Pointe's recorded declaration, which runs with the title to every lot, requires the Architectural Review Committee's written approval before any building, structure or other improvement, fences and landscaping included, is built, modified or altered, and lets the committee deny a change it reasonably finds out of harmony with its surroundings; it never mentions artificial turf or putting greens.
quote: all of which shall run with the title to such property and be binding upon all parties having any right, title, or interest in said property … Review. No buildings, structures or other Improvements including fences and landscaping shall be constructed, modified or altered unless first approved in writing by the Architectural Review Committee, provided however, that the Declarant and Builders whose plans and specifications have received Declarant's prior written approval shall be exempt from seeking or obtaining Architectural Review Committee approval during Declarant's or such Builder's development of, construction on, or sales of any Unit. The Architectural Review Committee shall exercise reasonable judgment to the end that all buildings, structures, modifications, alterations, or additions to the Units conform to and harmonize with existing surroundings and structures. The Architectural Review Committee has the absolute right to deny any requested buildings, structures, modifications, alterations, or additions which the Architectural Review Committee reasonably determines do not conform to and harmonize with existing surroundings and structures.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Preamble and Art. XI, Sec. 2 (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: The HOA posts a 50-page scan (the recorded declaration, 47 pages, plus the Feb. 25, 2002 Annexation and First Supplement, Reception No. 2927848, adding Filing Two Lots 1-4 of Block 1 and Outlot A). Read 2026-09-27 by OCR of every page (macOS Vision), with Art. XI pages checked against the page images. The words turf, artificial, synthetic, putting, green and lawn appear nowhere in the declaration, Exhibit B, the 2002 Rules and Regulations, the 2006 enforcement policy, the fee schedule or the architect review form. Declarant: Lot Holding Investments, LLC (the same declarant as Settlers Village).

fact: Colony Pointe's declaration counts landscaping and sprinkling systems as Improvements, and says the committee's Architectural Design Standards govern where improvements sit with respect to topography, finish grade elevation and the master drainage plan.
quote: Architectural Design Standards shall mean design standards adopted by the Architectural Review Committee from time to time that govern the quality of workmanship, color of materials, harmony of external design with existing structures, and location with respect to topography and finish grade elevation and the master drainage plan and all other appearances of buildings and structures in the Project. The Minimum Architectural Design Standards are set forth in Exhibit "B" attached hereto. … Improvements shall mean and refer to all improvements now or hereafter constructed including, without limitation, all buildings, exterior lighting, benches, walks, landscaping, sprinkling systems, irrigation ditches, and parking areas within the Project.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Art. I, Secs. 3 and 18 (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: Read by OCR of the recorded scan, 2026-09-27.

fact: Colony Pointe's covenants make each owner keep up the lot's grass and other landscaping and follow the mandatory landscaping requirements set in the Architectural Design Standards that the committee adopts and makes available; the HOA's posted documents include no standards beyond Exhibit B, which covers houses rather than yards.
quote: Each Owner shall provide prudent and regular exterior maintenance upon each Unit including painting, repairs and/or replacement of roofs, gutters, downspouts, exterior building surfaces, trees, shrubs, grass and other landscaping, walks, driveways and other surfaces, and all other exterior Improvements to maintain the value of said property. Owners shall comply with mandatory landscaping requirements as set forth in the Architectural Design Standards adopted by and available from the Architectural Review Committee.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Art. XI, Sec. 9(q)(i) (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: Read by OCR of the recorded scan and checked against the page image, 2026-09-27. Exhibit B (Minimum Architectural Design Standards, Secs. 1-11) covers styles, square footage, roof pitch, elevations, windows, exterior materials, colors, setbacks, site grading, paved areas and house plans; none of it is a landscaping requirement. The HOA documents page (colonypointehoa.com/hoa-documents) posts no separate Architectural Design Standards.

fact: Colony Pointe's covenants bar an owner from changing a lot's topography or drainage pattern without the committee's approval, hold each lot to the grading and design shown on the recorded plat, discourage large elevated decks or patios, and enforce the same building setbacks the Town of Milliken requires.
quote: Drainage. No Owner shall change the topography or drainage pattern of a Lot including, not by limitation, any drainage easement areas, from the topography or drainage pattern established by the Declarant unless such change is approved by the Architectural Review Committee. Any Owner who in any way materially modifies the topography or drainage pattern of a Lot without such consent shall be liable for any and all damages stemming therefrom, and may be required to return such topography or drainage patterns to their original state. … The design standards set forth herein are in addition to the requirements of the ordinances of the Town of Milliken. … Setbacks. The setbacks which will be enforced by the Architectural Review Committee are the same building setbacks that are required by the Town of Milliken, Colorado. Site Grading. Exterior grading shall be adequate for drainage away from the house and adjacent houses … The type of grading and design of each Lot is shown on the recorded Plat and must be adhered to. Houses shall be sited to complement existing or planned houses on adjacent sites. Large elevated decks or patios are discouraged.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Art. XI, Sec. 9(aa), and Exhibit B, Minimum Architectural Design Standards, Secs. 8 and 9 (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: Read by OCR of the recorded scan and checked against the page images (declaration p. 29; Exhibit B p. 1.3), 2026-09-27. The recorded plat (Final Plat, Reception No. 2802763, Oct. 26, 2000; Filing Two, Reception No. 2912142, Dec. 27, 2001) was not read.

fact: Colony Pointe's declaration asks an applicant for a site plan, complete construction plans, specifications with color schemes and material samples, and payment of anticipated review costs; gives the committee 30 days from a complete submittal to approve or reject in writing; deems the plans approved if it still has not answered 15 days after the applicant's certified-mail notice; and lets the committee inspect the finished work.
quote: Prior to commencement of any onsite work, the Owner or such Owner's designated representative (hereinafter referred to as "Applicant") must obtain the written approval of the Architectural Review Committee … The Applicant must submit to the Architectural Review Committee the following minimum items (in addition to other items which the Architectural Review Committee deems necessary or advisable for it to act under the circumstances): (i) Site plan; (ii) Complete construction plans; (iii) Specifications, including color schemes and material samples for the building, addition or alteration; and (iv) Payment in full of all anticipated costs as set forth below. … Upon receipt by the Architectural Review Committee of all items set forth above, the Architectural Review Committee shall thereafter have thirty (30) days to furnish Applicant with written notice of approval or rejection of the plans as submitted. If rejected, the Architectural Review Committee shall furnish a written explanation of the basis for its rejection and shall, if practical, furnish suggested modifications which would render the plans acceptable … If for any reason the Architectural Review Committee has not responded to the Applicant in writing within the thirty (30) day period as provided above, the Applicant shall notify the Architectural Review Committee of such failure in writing by certified mail, return receipt requested. Thereafter, unless the Architectural Review Committee furnishes written notice of approval or rejection as required above within fifteen (15) days following receipt of said notice from the Applicant, the plans as submitted shall be deemed approved. In the event the Architectural Review Committee has notified Applicant of the necessity of submitting additional documentation, the thirty (30) day and fifteen (15) day periods set forth above shall not begin until Applicant has submitted all required documentation. … Upon completion of the construction, modification or alteration of any Improvements, the Applicant shall furnish written notice to the Architectural Review Committee of same … Thereafter, the Architectural Review Committee or its designee shall have the right to inspect the Improvements to assure compliance with the approved plans … The Architectural Review Committee shall also have the power to require the Owner submitting matters to it for approval to pay reasonably necessary costs of the submission prior to their review and as a necessary condition thereof.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Art. XI, Secs. 4, 5 and 7 (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: Read by OCR of the recorded scan, 2026-09-27; the list markers (i)-(iv) are OCR-corrected from the page image.

fact: When the committee finds work out of compliance, including work begun without submitted plans, Colony Pointe's declaration requires the owner to stop and bring it into compliance within a reasonable time of no more than 30 days, and lets the committee seek an injunction, do the work at the owner's expense and recover damages, costs and attorney fees as a lien on the lot.
quote: If at any time the Architectural Review Committee determines an Owner or Applicant is not in compliance with the Architectural Design Standards or approved plans, including without limitation the failure to submit plans for approval prior to commencing any onsite work, the Architectural Review Committee shall furnish notice of noncompliance to the Owner. Upon such notice, the Owner shall immediately cease all work other than is required to bring the Improvements into compliance. If the Owner fails to immediately cease all such work, or fails to bring the Improvements into such compliance within a reasonable period of time not exceeding thirty (30) days, the Architectural Review Committee shall have all rights and remedies available pursuant to this Declaration, at law or in equity. … The Architectural Review Committee may seek appropriate injunctive relief in order to compel the Owner to cease all work and bring the Improvements into compliance or authorize the Architectural Review Committee to undertake all steps and actions, on the Owner's behalf and expense. Said expense shall be a personal obligation of the Owner and a charge and lien against said Owner's Unit as with Assessments as provided herein. … The Architectural Review Committee may recover from the Owner all damages, costs, and attorney fees suffered or incurred in connection with the existence or remedy of any Improvements found by a court of competent jurisdiction to be in noncompliance
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Art. XI, Sec. 6 (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: Read by OCR of the recorded scan, 2026-09-27. Damages, costs and attorney fees attach to Improvements that a court finds in noncompliance.

fact: Colony Pointe's declarant appointed the Architectural Review Committee only for an appointment period that ended no later than 10 years after the declaration was recorded; since then the association's Executive Board appoints the members, who may never number fewer than 3.
quote: The Architectural Review Committee shall consist of three (3) members, all of whom shall be appointed by Declarant. Declarant shall have the continuing right to appoint all three (3) members during the Appointment Period (as hereafter defined). The Association shall have the right to appoint such members after the end of the Appointment Period. The "Appointment Period" shall mean the period of time commencing as of the date of recordation of this Declaration and continuing until the earliest to occur of the following events: (a) when all Units in the Project have been conveyed to persons other than Declarant and certificates of occupancy have been issued for the residences constructed thereon; (b) ten (10) years after the date this Declaration is recorded; or (c) when, in its discretion, Declarant voluntarily relinquishes such right. … Members of the Architectural Review Committee to be appointed by the Association shall be appointed by the Executive Board. … After the Appointment Period, the Association may at any time and from time to time change the authorized number of members of the Architectural Review Committee, but the number of members of the Architectural Review Committee shall not be less than three (3).
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Art. XI, Sec. 3 (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: Read by OCR of the recorded scan and checked against the page image, 2026-09-27 (OCR misreads "carliest" and "(%)" corrected to "earliest" and "(b)"). Recorded Dec. 27, 2001, so the appointment period ended by Dec. 27, 2011 at the latest. Who sits on the committee now is not posted.

fact: Colony Pointe's covenants require the committee's written approval before any fence is built and written consent before a shed or other accessory building goes up, which is not to be unreasonably refused; require a dog run to be approved and kept out of sight of a street or public view; and allow no more than 3 dogs and 3 cats.
quote: Accessory Buildings. No accessory buildings, storage barns, or sheds shall be constructed or moved onto any Unit without written consent of the Architectural Review Committee. Said structures shall not be unreasonably prohibited so long as full consideration is given to architectural integration of materials, colors, and placement on the property. … No Owner may keep more than three (3) dogs and three (3) cats. … Clothes Lines and Dog Runs. No clothes lines shall be located on any Lot and dog runs must first be approved by the Architectural Review Committee and shall not be located on any Lot where they are visible from a street or public view. … Fencing. No fencing of any type shall be constructed by any Lot Owner on any Lot within the Project without prior approval in writing by the Architectural Review Committee.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Art. XI, Sec. 9(e), (i), (p) and (u) (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: Read by OCR of the recorded scan and checked against the page images (pp. 24-28), 2026-09-27. The covenants do not say whether a yard seen from Ehrlich Park's trail is in "public view"; pages hedge it.

fact: Colony Pointe's covenants allow no individual water supply system or sewage disposal system on any lot and require every house to attach to water and sewer under the Town of Milliken's ordinances and construction standards.
quote: Water and Sewer. No individual water supply system or sewage disposal system shall be permitted on any Unit and all dwellings must attach to water and sewer in conjunction with Town of Milliken ordinances and construction standards.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Colony Pointe Subdivision, Art. XI, Sec. 9(s) (recorded Dec. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2912045)
notes: Read by OCR of the recorded scan and checked against the page image (p. 28), 2026-09-27. No non-potable irrigation system for Colony Pointe lots was found in the HOA documents.

fact: The Colony Pointe HOA says the community has 233 single-family detached homes, has suspended dues for 2025, 2026 and 2027, will not provide status letters because of the board's limited availability, and says the Town owns and operates Ehrlich Park, Ehrlich Lake and the trails around them, a metro district, not the HOA, owns the green space along Alice Avenue, and owners maintain the house side of the wooden perimeter fence on Alice and Inez while the HOA handles the street side.
quote: Colony Pointe is a fantastic little community located in Milliken, CO and consists of 233 single family detached homes. … HOA dues for 2025 were suspended. As such, dues for 2026 have also been suspended and dues for 2027 are suspended at this time. … Due to limited availability of the HOA Board and HOA dues for 2025, 2026, and 2027 being suspended the HOA will not be providing Status Letters to title companies or homeowners. … The Green Space along Alice Avenue is owned and maintained by the … Metro District. … The wooden privacy fence along Alice and Inez are part of the HOA and Individual Homeowners. It is the Homeowners responsibility to maintain the house facing side of the fence. … The street facing side of the fence is the responsibility of the HOA and maintanence on the fence will be performed during the summer of 2023. … Who owns the trails and area around Ehrlich Park and Ehrlich Lake? The Town of Milliken owns and operates Ehrlich Park and Ehrlich Lake.
source_label: Colony Pointe HOA Milliken, home page and FAQ
notes: Read 2026-09-27. The HOA's count (233) differs from Weld County's 241 house lots (see milliken-co--colony-pointe.parcel-sizes); pages give both. The metro district's name is elided from the quote because its first word is a town name the site's checks refuse (territory.mjs TIMELESS_TOWNS); the Weld parcel roll lists it as Metropolitan District No. 1 of that family (see milliken-co--colony-pointe.outlots).

fact: The Colony Pointe HOA's documents page posts the covenants, an architect review form, the rules and regulations, an enforcement policy and a fee schedule, and asks owners to send architect review forms for paint by email.
quote: Colony Pointe HOA Information and Documents Send Architect Review Forms for Paint to colonypointehoamilliken@gmail.com. Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Colony Pointe HOA (pdf) … Architect Review Form (docx) … Rules and Regulation of Colony Pointe HOA (pdf) … Colony Pointe HOA Policy for Enforcement of Covenants and Rules (pdf) … Colony Pointe HOA Fee Schedule (pdf)
source_label: Colony Pointe HOA Milliken, HOA Documents page
notes: Read 2026-09-27. The page also posts bylaws, articles, a conflicts policy, a collections policy, 2023 and 2024 meeting minutes and the 2024 and 2025 budgets. It does not say where to send a landscape or fence application; the form itself lists mail or delivery to the HOA's post office box.

fact: The Colony Pointe HOA's application for architectural approval asks for a description of the work, including its size, color, materials and location, and at least one of plans, specifications such as a manufacturer's brochure, color or material samples, or photographs; says a form returned without a sample or plan will not be reviewed; commits the owner to no work before written approval and to a completion notice for inspection; and lists mail or delivery to the HOA's post office box.
quote: Description of Work (including design, nature, type, size, shape height, width, color, materials, and location of proposed improvements) … ONE OF THE FOLLOWING MUST BE SUBMITTED BEFORE YOUR REQUEST WILL BE REVIEWED: Plans including location, elevations, and dimensions Specifications (e.g. manufacturer’s brochure) Samples of colors Samples or description of materials Photographs … No work or commitment of work will be made by me until I have received written approval from the Association. … In the event of approval, I will notify the Architectural Control Committee in writing when the work is completed so that an inspection can be made to ensure that it conforms to what was approved. … I am aware that if I return this form incomplete, without a sample or plan, it will not be reviewed by the ARC. … Submission Options: Mail, Deliver to; Colony Pointe HOA P.O. Box 216 Milliken, Co 80543
source_label: Colony Pointe HOA, Application for Approval of Architectural Improvement (Architect Review Form)
notes: Read 2026-09-27 (Word file, converted to text). The form's checklist asks for one item; the declaration's Art. XI, Sec. 4(a) lists more (see milliken-co--colony-pointe.ccr-plan-review).

fact: The Colony Pointe HOA's fee schedule answers a first violation of its rules or covenants with a verbal or written warning, then $50, $100 and $150 for later offenses, and gives 72 hours after notice to correct it or send the board a corrective action plan.
quote: First Offense – Verbal or Written warning Second Offense - $50.00 Third Offense - $100.00 Fourth & Successive Offenses - $150.00 All violations shall be corrected or a corrective action plan be communicated to the HOA Board within 72 hours of notification of violation.
source_label: Colony Pointe HOA Fee Schedule
notes: Read 2026-09-27 (text PDF, undated). It differs from the 2006 enforcement policy (see milliken-co--colony-pointe.enforcement-policy) and from the 2002 Rules and Regulations ($15 a day after a hearing); pages say the documents differ and send owners to the board.

fact: Colony Pointe's 2006 enforcement policy lets the board assess a one-time fine of $100 to $5,000 for a violation not corrected in time and daily fines of $15 to $25 for a continuing one, after written notice and a chance to request a hearing in writing within four days.
quote: Fines. If an Owner fails to timely correct a violation, the Board has the right to assess a one-time fine in the amount of $100 to $5,000 (as the Board deems reasonable and necessary to promote correction of the violation). In addition, the Board may assess daily fines for any continuing or persistent violation in the amount of $15 to $25 per day (as the Board determines to be reasonable and necessary to promote correction of the violation) until the Owner has corrected the violation. … To request a hearing, the Owner must contact the Association in writing within four days after the effective date of the Notice.
source_label: Colony Pointe Homeowners Association, Policy for Enforcement of Covenants and Rules (effective Jan. 1, 2006)
notes: A scanned PDF, read 2026-09-27 by OCR of all 5 pages. It says it supersedes any earlier policy on the subject; the undated fee schedule posted beside it lists different amounts.

fact: At Colony Pointe's November 8, 2023 homeowners meeting, owners asked whether the HOA and the Town of Milliken could agree on fencing along the lake side, and poor maintenance of front landscaping was listed among ongoing covenant issues.
quote: Fencing along lake side - can HOA and Town of Milliken come to an agreement. … On going HOA Covenants Issues and Concerns a. Trailers on property (driveway) more than 72 hours. Vehicles parking on rocks. Poor maintenance of front landscaping.
source_label: Colony Pointe HOA, Homeowners Meeting Minutes, Nov. 8, 2023
notes: Read 2026-09-27 (text PDF). The minutes record the question, not an answer.

fact: At Colony Pointe's August 1, 2024 homeowners meeting, the future of the association was described as a covenant-style HOA with limited board member activity, and owners voted to stain the Alice and Inez perimeter fence in fall 2024, after which its upkeep would be the homeowners' responsibility.
quote: Discussion of future of HOA - covenant style HOA with limited board member activity. … Perimeter fence (Alice and Inez) - Homeowners have voted that staining take place in fall of 2024, at which time a letter will be sent to the homeowners that after the staining it will be the responsibility of the homeowner. … Need to confirm that there is not something in the contract of the homeowners that the fence is not an HOA maintenance.
source_label: Colony Pointe HOA, Homeowners Meeting Minutes, Aug. 1, 2024
notes: Read 2026-09-27 (text PDF). The HOA home page still says the street-facing side of that fence is the HOA's; the two documents differ, so pages send owners to the board.

fact: In a Milliken PUD, the approved master and final development plans control land use and may set standards, dimensions and uses that differ from the rest of the zoning code, and their maps and documents are recorded with the Weld County Clerk and Recorder and kept at the Town Clerk's office.
quote: development standards, dimensional requirements and permitted uses may be negotiated that are different from those set forth in this Chapter, and such different standards, dimensional requirements and uses, as negotiated, shall be allowed as set forth in the Master Development Plan (MDP) and Final Development Plan (FDP) … Land use and development within any PUD approved pursuant to these regulations shall be controlled by the provisions of the approved PUD MDP and FDP. Specific maps and documents detailing negotiated items and other matters related to these approved plans shall be recorded with the Weld County Clerk and Recorder and duplicate files of said plans and documents kept in the administrative offices of the Town Clerk.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-2-220(b) and (e)(2), Planned Unit Development District (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read 2026-09-27 through Municode's content API (product 18077, job 492897). Colony Pointe's PUD predates the current code (declaration recorded 2001); its development plan was not read.
